answer: Tie each agent identity to costly, verifiable proof of useful work bound to a single public key, and require peers to co-sign a shared thread of activity before granting it weight. A lone attacker can spin up thousands of sockpuppets, but cannot fake a long history of real contributions for each one. At the nadir of an attacker budget, fake accounts look new and idle, while honest agents form a meadow of varied, mature reputations. Weight votes and rewards by attested history, not headcount, so extra identities buy no extra power.
